messages.subject: Calverton / Ferncliffe - Wraysbury report query
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Dr Iqbal,

We act for Calverton Industries in a claim arising from the bar you tested (your report of 5 September 2025). Two questions as we prepare the letter before action: (1) are you able, if needed, to express a view on causation - i.e. that the corrosion failures are attributable to the low-molybdenum composition rather than to machining or installation? (2) would you be available to be instructed as an expert under CPR Part 35 if the matter proceeds?

Grateful for your initial view.

Tom Gallagher
Associate, Dispute Resolution
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 0148

Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: Calverton / Ferncliffe - Wraysbury report query
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Mr Gallagher,

Yes on both. On causation, the pitting morphology and the measured PREN of ~18 are entirely consistent with a 304-type material failing in a marine environment, and inconsistent with conforming 316L; I can deal with the machining/installation alternatives in a Part 35 report. I am able to act as expert subject to the usual conflict check and terms. Please send a formal letter of instruction when ready.

Kind regards
Faisal Iqbal
Wraysbury Materials Laboratory
